source_evidence: The bond’s market price will move up as interest rates move down and it will decline as interest rates rise, so that the market value of the bond may be more or less than the par value.
answer: Interest rate risk is the possibility that changing interest rates will affect a municipal bond’s market price. When interest rates rise, existing bonds’ market prices generally fall; when rates decline, their prices generally rise. This matters if you sell before the bond matures: a low fixed-rate municipal bond may be worth less in the market, and selling it could mean a loss. If held to maturity, the bond returns its face value, along with interest, according to the source.
